title: Speed-reduction gearbox
source: US Patent 1,770,035, Fig. 1 (public domain; held out before step 3)

metrics.scale: assumed: longest side of the drawing = 300 mm

steps.title: Planetary drive interpretation
steps.text: My reading is a compact planetary gear drive enclosed in a housing. Central sun gears drive surrounding planet gears that in turn engage outer wheels. The section view suggests a reduction drive for a heavy shaft.

steps.title: Housing holds everything
steps.text: The housing is formed by back covers and side walls that hold everything in alignment. Wall thickness is about 8.0 mm in model scale, real size unknown. The covers enclose the gear cluster while leaving the main shafts free to turn.

steps.title: Power enters centrally
steps.text: Power appears to enter along the central longitudinal shaft running through the housing. This shaft carries the inner sun gears and spins them within the planet cluster. Rotation is supported by end plates and bearings around the shaft line.

steps.title: Gear train meshes
steps.text: Motion passes from the sun gears to planet gears and onward to the outer gears. The mesh between sun and planet by measured geometry is shown by close axis spacing, while other meshes were guessed by the engineer to complete the train. The ratio is unknown because the teeth were not counted, with tooth counts only guessed in the model.

steps.title: Output wheels turn
steps.text: The final motion leaves through the large outer wheels that rotate about the main axis. The left wheel measures 132.7 mm across and the upper wheel measures 79.8 mm across in model scale, real size unknown. These wheels turn slowly relative to the central shaft and deliver the output torque.

steps.title: Guessed details explained
steps.text: Plate thickness and housing depth were guessed because the drawing gives only edge views without values. Depth reaches 338.4 mm in model scale, real size unknown. Shafts and bearings and base blocks were added by the engineer because gears and wheels showed no axles and the frame could not stand alone.
